Depending on the exchange center and instrument you select, you will have one or more order types to choose from: Market Order: A market order is a request to buy or sell a security at the best-available price in the current market. It guarantees an execution but not the exact price. Also called an order without limit. Limit Order: A limit order allows an order to be matched at a specified price. For equities, the limit is always given as a price per share, while for bonds it is a percentage of the face value. The limit sets the maximum price for a buy order and the minimum price for a sell order, meaning the prices at which each order should be executed. We recommend that you always specify a limit. Stop-limit buy/sell order: For a stop-limit buy order, the trigger limit (“stop-limit“) and the limit must be above the current market price. The trigger limit determines when the order will be activated for the relevant trading system. When the current market price reaches or exceeds the trigger limit, the order is entered into the trading system and treated as a limited order. The limit is the highest price at which the order is to be executed and must be greater than or equal to the trigger limit. For a stop-limit sell order, the trigger limit (“stop-limit“) and the limit must be below the current market price. The trigger limit determines when the order will be activated for the relevant trading system. When the current market price reaches or falls below the trigger limit, the order is entered into the trading system and treated as a limited order. The limit is the lowest price at which the order is to be executed and must be less than or equal to the trigger limit. On-stop order (buy) / stop-loss order (sell): An on-stop/stop-loss order is an order to buy or sell a security when it reaches a certain price. This order guarantees a pre-determined price but not an execution. For an on-stop order the trigger limit must be higher than the current price, and for a stop-loss order it must be lower.

This order guarantees a pre-determined price but not an execution. For an on-stop order the trigger limit must be higher than the current price, and for a stop-loss order it must be lower. When the current market price reaches the trigger, the order is submitted to the trading system without a limit (“at best“). In this learning path, you will learn the basics for easy management of your money, targeted retirement planning and smart investing. Women who take their finances into their own hands lay the foundation for an independent and self-determined life. A solid financial foundation is the beginning of every journey. It’s the backpack that contains everything essential to reach your destination safe and sound. No matter what your individual path looks like: Every stage in life and all your wishes and goals have different financial implications. That’s why it’s important to protect yourself, save for retirement and build up assets to be well-positioned for all of life’s events and achieve your goals. Laying the foundation: the “Financial basics” learning path provides readers with valuable basic knowledge about money and finance in five modules. In this way, you can achieve financial stability in everyday life, save for a self-determined future and build up assets. Each learning path module offers varied and practical expertise as well as lots of tips and tools so you can put what you’ve learned into practice right away.

Module 1 – Initial goals: how to take your future into your own hands
Standing on your own two feet financially for the first time is a big responsibility, but also an opportunity to live life on your own terms. Find out how you can best prepare for this and lay the groundwork for financial independence.

Module 2 – Save with a plan: to make both big and small wishes come true
How do you budget to stay in the black? A solid budget plan will help you set yourself up for financial success today, tomorrow and in the long run. This will bring you closer to your goals step by step.

Module 3 – Save for retirement: secure your future and save on taxes
No matter where you are in life, maintain your desired standard of living in retirement – and save on taxes today. Targeted retirement saving pays off in several ways. We show you what’s important.

Module 4 – Invest with foresight: how to achieve your long-term goals
Learn the basics of investing to make more of your money in the long term – for your own future and for what matters to you.

Module 5 – Looking to the future: how to lay the foundation for a fulfilled life
Career, family or both? No matter where your journey takes you, financial security and independence are the cornerstones of your success. Find out how to optimize your finances for the future. A learning path comprises various types of content, tips and tools related to an overarching topic. The goal is to build up your financial knowledge step by step. A learning path consists of multiple modules. Each module deals with a specific sub-topic. The modules can be accessed independently of one another, so you can pause your learning journey and resume it at any time. Each module is dedicated to a specific topic from the overarching learning path topic. After a short introduction, you will receive helpful expert knowledge in the form of articles and tools that are both easy to understand and practical. In this way, you can build up knowledge on a specific topic in a targeted manner. Yes, you can register for as many learning paths as you like. You decide whether you want to follow one learning path at a time, or more than one in parallel. The “Financial basics” learning path is an ideal gateway to all the other topics. You’ll receive confirmation by email. This lists all the learning paths you have registered for. You’ll receive a separate email with the links to the individual modules for each learning path. This will take you to the topic you’re currently interested in with one click.

Our credit cards and prepaid cards use state-of-the-art technology and meet the highest security standards . We also apply the maximum level of security when it comes to online payments. We recommend the following when using your cards: Cover the keypad with your free hand or your purse or wallet when entering your PIN. Keep your PIN secret and do not let anyone watch you entering it. We have summarized the most important rules for the secure use of our cards in our security guidelines . Making contactless payments with our cards is easy, practical and fast. All you need to do is hold the card briefly against the card reader. The card stays in your hand during the entire transaction Data can only be transmitted from the card chip if it is held close to the reader. Only one transaction is possible at a time, as the security chip generates a unique code for each transaction. Any attempt to use a code more than once or to use an incorrect code is detected immediately. For amounts over CHF 80 , you also need to enter your PIN (this is automatically requested). For even greater security: Before making your first contactless payment, you must complete a transaction where you insert the card into the payment terminal and enter your correct PIN. The contactless function is then activated automatically, and you can make contactless payments. If your card is lost or stolen, block it immediately . Cards can also be blocked via E-Banking and Mobile Banking. Blocking a credit card Blocking a debit card

Find our current KeyClub point collection rules at the following link: Points are calculated on the basis of the total spending on your quarterly credit card statements (e.g. January to March) based on the billing date of the statement – minus cash withdrawals, digital currency purchases, credit card fees, lottery/betting/casino transactions and transfers. Points are only credited if the minimum amount of 10 collected points has been reached. If you have collected fewer than 10 KeyClub points, these will be carried over to the next period. Intro text: Here we show you how to set up widgets and shortcuts on your smartphone to make payments with UBS TWINT even easier. Good to know: You can also select shortcuts like "pay" by long-pressing the app symbol. With a widget on the lock screen, you can have access to various UBS TWINT functions at your fingertips. For example, quick access to the QR code scanner. How to set up widgets: Long-press the lock screen and then tap "Customize". Select the lock screen you wish to customize and tap the area under the time; the "Add widgets" menu will appear. Search in the app list for UBS TWINT. Select the UBS TWINT widget you want and drag it to the widget area. Save by tapping "Done. With a widget on the home screen, you have faster access to UBS TWINT functions, like paying, sending money, requesting money or paying for parking. How to set up widgets: Long-press an empty area on the home screen of your iPhone. Tap the "+" symbol on the top-left part of the screen. Search in the app list for UBS TWINT. Select the UBS TWINT widget you want and tap "Add widget" or drag it to the area you want it on your home screen. You can open your favorite TWINT functions even quicker with UBS TWINT controls on your lock screen. Unlike widgets on the lock screen, these controls replace the standard camera and flashlight controls. Good to know: You can still access the camera quickly by swiping from right to left on the lock screen—even without the camera control. This means you can safely replace the camera control with a UBS TWINT control. How to set up controls on the lock screen: Touch and hold the lock screen for a few seconds, then click “Customize”. Select the lock screen you want to adjust and then click the “-” symbol next to the control that you would like to replace (camera and flashlight are configured by default). Click the now-empty control slot and search for UBS TWINT in the controls gallery. Select the UBS TWINT control you want to add. To save your changes, click “Done”. Discover three easy ways to quickly open the UBS TWINT QR code scanner – with shortcuts or by tapping the back of your iPhone.

Select the UBS TWINT control you want to add. To save your changes, click “Done”. Discover three easy ways to quickly open the UBS TWINT QR code scanner – with shortcuts or by tapping the back of your iPhone. To set up a Siri shortcut to open the QR code scanner, you can follow these steps: Open the Shortcuts app on your iPhone. Tap the "+" symbol top right and select "Add action". Search for UBS TWINT and select "Pay". Tap "Done" to save. With your iPhone 15 or newer, you can also set the Action Button to trigger a saved Shortcut like "Pay". Follow these steps to set up the Action Button in this way: Go to Settings on your iPhone and search for "Action Button". Select "Shortcut" as the action that you want the Action Button to trigger. Then select your newly created "Pay" shortcut and save. Now you can simply press the Action Button and quickly and easily pay with UBS TWINT. For older iPhones, you can set it up so it opens the QR code scanner when you tap the back of the iPhone. Here's how it works: Go to Settings on your iPhone and search for "Back Tap". Tap the "Back Tap" setting and then select "Double Tap". Scroll down and search under "Shortcuts" for "Pay". Close the settings and try it out by tapping twice on the back of your iPhone – now the UBS TWINT QR code scanner should open. With the tiles function, you can more comfortably access UBS TWINT and its functions. And you can do this directly from the lock screen by opening the notification center there. On certain Android models, you can also place the tiles directly on the lock screen to access UBS TWINT functions even faster. How to set up tiles: Swipe down to open the notification center and then swipe again to open all tiles for Quick Settings. Now swipe left until you see a plus icon, a pencil icon, or an edit button. Look for the UBS TWINT tiles. Drag the UBS TWINT tile you want to add to the available tile area. With a widget on the home screen, you have faster access to the various UBS TWINT app functions. If you sell a property before you reach statutory retirement age, you must repay the advance withdrawal of vested benefits. The repayment is made to the current pension fund, which will confirm the repayment of the advance withdrawal and create the request to cancel the sale restriction. If the advanced withdrawal cannot be repaid before the property is sold, an irrevocable promise to pay is required. The bank or notary will confirm the amount to be transferred to the collective account (CH81 0023 0230 1011 8870 0) of the UBS Vested Benefits Foundation AG (important for repayment: Note VB account number/ last name / first name / “EHO repayment”). If the repayment is expressly recorded in the purchase contract, no additional promise of payment is required. You can withdraw funds from your vested benefits account to purchase property. If funds are withdrawn, the law requires that a “sales restriction” note be made in the land registry. This means that the purchased property can be sold before you reach statutory retirement age if the sales restriction has been removed by the provider. This sales restriction can be removed, upon request, in the following cases: from 5 years before statutory retirement age (59 for women and 60 for men) when you’ve repaid the money you withdrew early on when you have an irrevocable promise to pay if you cannot make the repayment before the sale upon transfer to a new property serving as your new main place of residence. If the advance withdrawal was not made with the UBS Vested Benefits Foundation AG, the foundation requires information on the ownership structure, land register sheet, municipality and the amount (e.g., with a copy of the sales restriction) to remove the restriction. If you sell a property and buy another one, and this property becomes your main place of residence, the existing sales restriction in the land registry must be deleted and another one must be entered for the new property. It's crucial to provide information on the previous property's ownership structure, land registry sheet, municipality (e.g., with a copy of the sales restriction), the new property and the amount (e.g., with a tax notification or a statement from the EHO withdrawal). An official certified purchase contract and a declaration of consent are also required for entering the sales restriction of a new property in the land registry. The sales restriction on the previous property will then be removed and a new one registered for the new property.

Financial requirements: First, create an overview of your expenses after retirement. Remember that some of these could increase, e.g., health, leisure, home repair/maintenance costs. Pension or lump sum: As a rule, you can choose whether you’d like to draw your pension fund assets as a monthly pension or have the full amount paid out. Some pension funds also offer a combination of both (partial withdrawal). Early retirement: Also consider the possibility of early retirement. Pension fund purchase: A pension fund purchase is particularly worthwhile in the years leading up to retirement. This is because the tax-savings effect of a pension fund purchase is the greatest when income is at its highest. For many employed persons, this is the case in the years immediately before retirement.

Payment of vested benefits assets in the event of death
Order of beneficiaries In the event of death, vested benefits are paid out according to the order of beneficiaries laid down in law (Art. 15 OLP/FZV). Retirement savings do 
not constitute an inheritance claim and are therefore not part of the estate. The groups are prioritized in the following order. This means that e.g., persons in Group 2 will only receive capital if persons in Group 1 do not exist. If there are multiple beneficiaries in the same Group, capital is divided up equally between them. Group 1: the surviving spouse or registered partner; under-age children; children with a full IV pension or in education up to the maximum age of 
25; divorced spouse Group 2: the person who cohabited with the deceased for an uninterrupted period of five years until their death; persons who must provide for the 
maintenance of one or more mutual children; natural persons who were receiving considerable financial support from the deceased pension account 
holder Group 3: children of full age who do not meet the conditions listed in Group 1 or, in their absence the parents, or in their absence the siblings Group 4: other legal heirs (according to the certificate of inheritance), excluding any payments due to the state or municipal institutions Details of the deceased pension account holder1 Last name Street, no.

In this learning path, you’ll discover the essentials relating to buying, owning and selling real estate. And you’ll learn to approach the entire process – from financing to transferring the property – in a structured and well-prepared manner. Women who are knowledgeable about real estate processes make informed decisions, bringing them closer to the dream of owning their own property. When it comes to buying, owning and selling residential property and investing in real estate, numerous financial, legal and strategic considerations play a key role. By getting to grips with these aspects of real estate, you can avoid the pitfalls and achieve your personal dreams regarding your living situation and your investment goals. In the “real estate” learning path, our expert Anna guides you through six informative modules and shares valuable knowledge at every stage of the real estate process. You’ll receive a structured overview – from financing and finding a property through to ownership and transfer – as well as insights into real estate as an investment. Each module provides practical tips, helpful checklists and useful tools that you can directly apply to your real estate project.

Module 1 – Establish the foundation: how to realize your dream of owning real estate
What does it take to buy a property? In this module, you’ll learn which first steps are useful, which questions you should ask yourself and your partner (if applicable) and how to translate your wishes into realistic goals.

Module 2 – Clarify the financing: how to find the right solution
Mortgage, equity, affordability – what exactly do these terms mean? Learn about the different financing models, what’s important with regard to borrowing and how buying a property or a condominium will affect your finances in the long term.

Module 3 – Purchase property: how to find and buy the right property
From the viewing to the purchase agreement: which criteria are decisive? And what affects the price? Learn how to find the right property, accurately assess its market value and ensure the purchase process goes smoothly.

Module 4 – Investing in real estate: how to use real estate as an investment
Real estate as an investment offers various opportunities – but also different challenges, depending on the strategy chosen. This module shows you the options you have for investing in real estate and how to use a property as a long-term investment.

Module 5 – Owning real estate: how to ensure the long-term value of your property
Ownership means obligations: This module explains how to maintain the value of your property through energy-efficient renovations, what maintenance costs arise and what you should watch out for to enjoy your home in the long term.

Module 6 – Changing ownership: how to sell or transfer your property
Whether you’re selling to third parties or passing property on within the family – sooner or later a change of ownership is inevitable. Here you’ll learn which steps are necessary, which tax aspects you should consider and how to make sure the process goes smoothly. A learning path contains a selection of content, tips and tools on a broad topic. The aim: building up and expanding financial knowledge step by step. The learning path consists of several modules. Each module covers a specific subtopic. The content can be accessed independently of the other modules. This means you can easily take a break from your learning journey and resume it at any time. Each module is dedicated to a specific topic within the overarching learning path theme. After a brief introduction, you’ll receive helpful expert knowledge through articles and tools – set out in an easy-to-understand and practical manner. In this way you build up targeted knowledge on the specific topic. Yes, you can sign up for as many learning paths as you like. You decide whether you want to go through the learning paths in order or in parallel. The “finance basics” learning path offers an ideal introduction to all the other topics. You’ll receive a confirmation email. This lists all the learning paths you’ve signed up for. You’ll receive a separate email for each learning path containing links to the individual modules. With just one click, you can access the topic that interests you.

How does UBS Manage Advanced [My Way] work?
How does UBS Manage Advanced [My Way] work? Based on your individual investment concept, we define an appropriate strategy. Together, we create your individual portfolio from around 80 different investment building blocks. We take care of the daily management within the building blocks and your overall portfolio, including risk monitoring. If your needs change, we will adjust your portfolio together with you at any time. Via Digital Banking, you can change allocations to your building blocks yourself.

Three ways to organize your home screen
Three ways to organize your home screen Arrange widgets Add a widget Remove a widget

Arrange widgets
1. On your home screen , touch and hold the widget you'd like to move. 2. Drag the widget to a new location. The widget’s location has been set.

Add a widget
1. Scroll to the bottom of your home screen . 2. Tap the Edit home screen button 3. Under Available widgets , choose the widget you would like to add. 4. Choose Save . The widget now appears on your home screen .

Remove a widget
1. From your home screen , touch and hold the widget you’d like to remove. 2. In the pop-up menu, choose Remove widget . 3. Then tap Remove . The widget no longer appears on your home screen .

text: Important: Before we can instruct you on how to activate 3-D Secure (3DS), first we need to know if you have E-Banking and Mobile Banking. Simply select below which situation applies to you. Tip: If you have received a card requested from a partner or a member of your family please proceed to the 3DS for a partner card page .

How to activate 3DS on a personal card
How to activate 3DS on a personal card I don’t have E-Banking or Mobile Banking I have E-Banking or Mobile Banking

Part 1 of 3: Start by signing up for E-Banking & Mobile Banking
1. Download the Access App 2. Open the Access App and tap on I only have a card 3. A mobile browser window will open – register your card for E-Banking by filling in all details and tap Submit Your card is now being registered for E-Banking and Mobile Banking. Important: Your new contract number will either be sent via SMS immediately, or you will receive it in a letter in a few business days. When you have received it, continue to Part 2.

Part 2 of 3: Continue with the details you’ve been sent
4. Return to the Access App 5. In the Access App, enter the SMS code 6. To confirm the activation, enter your Credit card PIN Your details are now confirmed. Continue to Part 3. 4. Open the Access App again 5. In the Access App, enter the contract number from your letter 6. Enter the activation code from the activation letter and tap Next Your details are now confirmed. Continue to Part 3.

Part 3 of 3: Finish the activation of 3-D Secure
7. Choose a Device name and tap Next 8. Set your Access App PIN and tap Confirm 9. Recommended: Allow push notifications by tapping on Set up now 3DS is now activated on your credit card and you can shop online securely. You can also access your bills, transactions, and card limits in E-Banking or Mobile Banking at any time.

Is your card in your E-Banking?
Log in to E-Banking . If your card is visible, you’re all set! 3DS is already activated on your card. You can shop online securely. You can also access your bills, transactions, and card limits in E-Banking or Mobile Banking at any time.

Part 1 of 2: Start by registering your card in E-Banking
1. Login to E-Banking on your computer 2. Click on Cards, then on Settings for cards 3. Scroll to the Credit Cards section and click Manage cards 4. Then click on + Add card 5. Fill in your new card number and your Date of Birth, and then click on Register You will receive a letter with a PIN. This may take a few days. When you have received the PIN, come back and continue the registration below.

Part 2 of 2: Finish by confirming your registration
6. Return to the Manage cards screen (as seen in step 03) 7. Enter the PIN code sent to your company 8. Click on Activate to confirm you registration and complete the activation 3DS is now activated on your credit card and you can shop online securely. You can also access your bills, transactions, and card limits in E-Banking or Mobile Banking at any time.

Problem not solved?
Problem not solved? You can just as easily connect a debit card to your E-Banking or Mobile Banking and start using the Access App for confirming your online purchases. All you need is to activate the option for online shopping. The activation process is slightly different if you received a card from your partner or a family member. You’ll then need to follow the process of activating a partner card .

In Switzerland, salary components above CHF 136,080 may be insured in a 1e plan. The name refers to article 1e of the Federal Law on Occupational Retirement, Survivors’ and Disability Pension Plans (BVV 2). The main advantage for 1e plan participants is that they can choose the investment strategy for their pension assets in the 1e plan themselves. As a result, the investment strategy can be regularly adapted to a person’s personal risk capacity and individual investment horizon. UBS offers two distinct 1e solutions, each tailored to the needs of different target customer segments: UBS 1e Collective Foundation: This solution is designed for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). It enables companies to implement flexible and efficient 1e plans tailored to their specific needs. UBS Optio 1e Collective Foundation: This solution is aimed at large, multinational companies. It offers comprehensive and customizable options to meet the complex needs of global organizations. To find out more about which solution is best for your company and to get in touch with the right contact person, please visit our dedicated 1e pension solutions page .

To protect your account, new payees must be confirmed once in E-Banking or the Mobile Banking App using the Access App or Access Card. This extra step helps prevent fraud and keeps your transactions safe. Key points about confirming payees How do I confirm a payee?

Why confirm a payee?
A confirmed payee is someone you authorize to receive payments. You confirm the payee when making the first payment. Future payments to the same payee don’t require confirmation. This ensures only trusted recipients can receive your funds.

Why review your payee list?
Check your confirmed payees regularly to stay in control. This reduces the risk of unauthorized transactions. You will find your list in E-Banking under Payments > Payees and invoicing parties. To view only your confirmed recipients, select the “Confirmed payees” filter under “Categories”. To remove a recipient from the list, click the three-dots and select “Revoke confirmation”.

Why am I asked to assess the payment for potential fraud?
This step is an important layer of protection for your account. Fraudsters often use persuasive tactics to trick people into making payments to unauthorized recipients. The Access App also provides specific tips based on the payment purpose to help you identify potential fraud quickly.

Can I pay someone without confirmation?

How do I set up a confirmation limit?
Navigate in the top right to “Settings > Security settings” and then left in the menu to “Confirmation of payees”, and adjust the limit. Navigate to “Profile > Settings > Security > Set up monthly transfer limit” and adjust the limit under “Limit for payments without confirmation of new payees”.

What if I see an unauthorized payee?
Act fast: Revoke the confirmation Check your payment history Contact UBS Digital Banking support immediately

Do I need to confirm health insurance?
Some payees, such as health insurance companies or telecommunications companies, have already been confirmed by UBS.

What are reserved amounts and what can I do about them?
What are reserved amounts and what can I do about them? Reserved amounts are provisional charges that are still being processed. These amounts are shown in red with a clock symbol in your E-Banking. If you have been charged twice for the same purchase, you can only dispute the amount once it has been definitively charged to your account. Click here to find out how to dispute an amount that has been charged twice.

Reserved amounts for card transactions
Reserved amounts for card transactions Reserved amounts for card transactions may be higher than the amount actually charged. At gas stations and for hotel reservations or car rentals – for example in connection with a deposit or security deposit – these amounts are reserved for seven days. Only the actual outstanding billing amount is definitively charged.

Reserved amounts when buying flight tickets
Reserved amounts when buying flight tickets When buying flight tickets, it may look like the airline has charged the amount twice. Actually, the second charge is just a reserved amount to check the creditworthiness of customers. UBS does not have any influence over how such charges are processed or how long the amount actually remains reserved (see also the "Terms and conditions for the use of UBS Debit Cards" section 10). This may be as long as 30 days. Please contact the airline directly if you have any questions.

To request a payout of your vested benefits, you need several official documents. The following explanations indicate where you can order the documents, their contents, what they're called abroad and where you can order them abroad. Civil status certificate (no older than 3 months): this document provides your current personal data such as your name and civil status. Family record document (marriage certificate): this document confirms the place and date of marriage and contains the current personal details of the husband, wife and children from their marriage. The family record document is reissued each time an event affects your civil status (e.g., birth, death, registration of a child). Civil partnership certificate: this document confirms the place and date of a registered partnership and the names and domiciles of the partners before and after registration. Registration notice from the Swiss resident’s registration office (deregistration date no earlier than one year prior) or residence certificate from abroad (issuing date no earlier than 3 months prior)*: this document states the registered person's place of residence at the time of departure from Switzerland to move abroad. Certificate of inheritance: The certificate of inheritance discloses information about the heirs and is required to gain access to inheritance. Registered civil status document (issue date as of date of death): This document discloses information about the registered person's parents, spouses and children. Swiss citizens can order the respective documents (civil status certificate, family record, civil partnership certificate) at the civil register office in their hometown. Those who are not Swiss citizens can order these statements at the civil register office closest to their current or previous domicile address. You must request confirmation of place of residence / declaration certificate / certificate of departure in your current domicile (for both citizens and non-citizens). A certificate of inheritance or proof of a deceased pensioner's registered civil status can be picked up at the inheritance office. If you are no longer a resident in Switzerland, please see below for the list of documents required instead of the civil status certificate and confirmation of place of residence in several other countries. Swiss citizens abroad can get these documents in the consulate of the country in which they live.

text: On this learning path, you will find out how the Swiss pension system works, where gaps can potentially arise and how you can effectively close these gaps. Seven out of ten women recommend actively starting to save for your retirement at an early stage. If you do so, you will enjoy more financial independence in the long term – including in your old age. Many people continually put off the issue of pension provision – be that due to uncertainty, a lack of knowledge or a feeling that it can wait. However, this can often lead to unpleasant surprises later in life. Women in particular are frequently at a disadvantage when it comes to pension provision: periods out of work, part-time employment and lower salaries mean that they receive far less from the various pension pillars than men. By getting a clear picture at an early stage, it is possible to identify gaps and purposefully utilize potential for optimization. This will give you more financial independence in the long term and enable you to maintain your accustomed standard of living in old age. In the “Retirement” learning path, expert Anna guides you through five practical modules and shows you how you can purposefully optimize your pension provision . You will be given a structured overview of the Swiss pension system and its three pillars. You will also learn about specific measures for various phases of life . Every module offers in-depth expertise, useful checklists and helpful tools and calculators that you can use directly for your pension planning and to prepare for your retirement.

Module 1 – Understanding the Swiss pension system and making the right decisions for your future
What are the different pillars? And what is their purpose? In this module, you will find out how the pension system is structured, why it affects everyone and why taking action early is particularly worthwhile.

Module 2 – Optimizing pillar 1: state pension provision (AHV/IV/EO)
You can easily check your personal situation with respect to old-age and survivors’ insurance (AHV). Find out how the AHV works, how your pension is calculated and what to watch out for to avoid contribution gaps.

Module 3 – Optimizing pillar 2: occupational pension provision
Do you know what your pension fund statement reveals about your pension provision? In this module, you will learn what matters in the second pillar and how to make optimal use of your pension fund for your retirement.

Module 4 – Utilizing pillar 3: closing gaps with private pension savings
With the third pillar, you not only secure your standard of living in old age, but can also take advantage of tax benefits. Learn how to approach this smartly to unlock the full potential offered by voluntary pension provision.

Module 5 – Start your retirement planning early: your roadmap
Whether you are only just starting out or are approaching retirement: this module shows you how to put together a pension plan at an early stage, close gaps in your pension provision and address important topics like succession planning in plenty of time. Learning paths are made up of various content items, tips and tools for an overriding topic. The goal is to build up and expand your financial knowledge on a step-by-step basis. The learning path consists of several modules, with each module focusing on a specific sub-topic. Content items can be accessed independently of one another. This means that you can take a break at any point and return to your learning path whenever you want. Modules are dedicated to specific topics from the overriding theme of the learning path. After a short introduction, you will be provided with useful specialist knowledge via articles and tools – compiled in an easily understandable and practical manner. This enables you to build up your knowledge of the specific topic in a targeted way. Yes, you can sign up for as many learning paths as you want. You decide for yourself whether you want to complete the learning paths successively or in parallel. The “Financial basics” learning path provides an ideal foundation for all the other topics. You will receive a confirmation by e-mail listing all the learning paths that you have signed up for. For each learning path, you will receive a separate e-mail with the links to the individual modules. All you have to do is click on these to get to the topic you are currently interested in.

Key points at a glance.
The following layout rules and recom-
mendations refer to all three versions  
of the payment part and receipt: 
–  integrated in a QR-bill in paper form
–  as an enclosure to a QR-bill in paper form –  integrated in a QR-bill for bills sent 
electronically (e.g. by e-mail), such  
as in PDF format Paper format and quality
The payment part and receipt must be 
printed in DIN A6/5 landscape format 
(210 x 105 mm) on natural white or white 
paper with a weight of at least 80 to 
maximum 100 g/m2. The use of certified 
recycled, FSC and TCF papers is permit-
ted. Neither coated nor reflecting stand-
ard paper may be used. The layout rules for the payment part 
apply regardless of whether it is inte-
grated in a bill or enclosed with it. Positioning of the payment part  
and receipt 
If the payment part with receipt are inte-
grated as part of a QR-bill, they must be 
positioned at the lower edge. Fonts, font color and sizes 
The following sans-serif fonts are  
permitted: 
–  Arial 
–  Frutiger 
–  Helvetica 
–  Liberation Sans 
The font color is always black. Type may 
not be in italic nor underlined. Font sizes, payment part 
The title "Payment part" must be in 11 pt 
(bold). The font size for the headings  
and their values is between 6 pt and  
10 pt for the "Amount" and the "Details" 
(see overview on page 6), with the font 
size for the values being 2 pt bigger than  
that for the heading. 5 We recommend that you use font size  
8 pt for the headings and 10 pt for the 
corresponding values. The exception,  
in font size 11 pt (bold), is the title "Pay-
ment part". The font size for the alterna-
tive procedure is 7 pt. Font sizes, receipt 
The font sizes for the receipt are 6 pt for 
the headings (bold) and 8 pt for the 
associated values. The exception, in font 
size 11 pt (bold), is the title "Receipt".

Key points at a glance.
The exception, in font 
size 11 pt (bold), is the title "Receipt". Languages to choose from 
The payment part with receipt can be 
produced in the following languages: 
–  German 
–  French 
–  Italian 
–  English 
The biller is free to choose which  
language to use. IBAN and customer references 
The QR reference is arranged in groups 
of 5 characters and the Creditor Reference 
in groups of 4. The IBAN is also arranged 
in groups of 4 characters, but differently: 
the QR reference is right-justified while 
the IBAN and Creditor Reference are 
left-justified. –  Sample QR reference: 
  21 00000 00003 13947 14300 09017 
–  Sample SCOR reference 
(Creditor Reference): 
  RF18 5390 0754 7034 
–  Sample IBAN: 
  CH43 3199 9000 0012 6578 9 Sizes and dimensions 
The following illustrations are to scale 
(1:1) in millimeters. Please note that when this document  
is printed out, the whole A4 format  
is slightly reduced so the dimensions 
shown here may no longer be com-
pletely accurate.

If you meet all criteria, this is how you use "Pay later": First, make sure that "Pay later" is activated . If it is activated, you will see a "Pay later" message when you initiate payments to merchants that offer "Pay later" as a payment method. By choosing this message, you can change the payment method to “Pay later”. The first time you select "Pay later" to make a purchase, you will need to register with Swissbilling, which offers this service. Once you are registered, you can simply use "Pay later" as a payment method for future purchases – whenever it is offered by the merchant.

Security
Security If your smartwatch is lost or stolen, please immediately delete your UBS Credit Card or Prepaid Card in the manufacturer's app. This does not block your physical card, and you can continue to use it. Further Information
Further Information The payment function is based on tokenization technology. When the UBS Credit Card or Prepaid Card is registered, a token is generated (comparable to an alias for the 16-digit credit card number). This token is then stored on your smartwatch on a specially secured chip. For payments at card terminals, the token is assigned to the 16-digit credit card number in the background by credit card networks (Mastercard & Visa). The payments are then processed using the existing credit card networks, and the assigned, physical credit card or prepaid card is charged. The payments appear on your monthly statement like other credit card transactions from the same credit card or prepaid card. The payment service is exclusively provided to you by smartwatch manufacturers or the providers of the smartwatch payment solution. They are also responsible for the availability of the payment service as well as technical support. With Zurich Immo-Protect, you can insure against the financial risks of death or incapacity to work. You decide what risk you want to insure against (death/incapacity to work/both) and choose the amount of the lump-sum payment. Life insurance: in the event of death, the insured capital is paid out immediately. Insurance against incapacity to work: in the event of incapacity to work, Zurich covers the premium payment for the insurance after a waiting period of 12 months. On 25 September 2022, the AHV 21 reform was approved by the Swiss electorate – this affects both occupational and private pensions. The reform provides for changes to the reference age, early withdrawal and deferral of retirement benefits. The statutory retirement age for women will be gradually increased from 64 to 65 years. The AHV 21 reform will come into force on 1 January 2024.

Gradual increase in the reference age for women of the transitional generation
Gradual increase in the reference age for women of the transitional generation For women of the transitional generation (born between 1961 and 1964), the reference age will be gradually increased as shown in the table below. For women born in 1964 whose entitlement to vested benefits arose in 2023 at the age of 59, the option of early withdrawal will not be lost when AHV 21 comes into force. Women born in 1965 or later are entitled to withdraw their vested benefits early at age 60. Example I: A woman (born 3 May 1965) turned 58 in the year 2023. She would like to withdraw her vested benefits in 2024 at the age of 59. She may do so at the earliest in 2025 at the age of 60 (from 3 May 2025). Example II: A woman born on 30 November 1961 can withdraw her vested benefits until 31 December 2029 without proof of gainful employment. She can continue to postpone the withdrawal until 28 February 2031 (69 years and 3 months) under the condition that she provides proof of gainful employment.

Deferral of withdrawal of vested benefits (women and men)
Currently, withdrawal of vested benefits may be deferred for up to five years beyond the statutory retirement age, i.e., up to a maximum age of 69 for women and 70 for men. It does not matter whether the person continues in gainful employment or not. After the transitional period has passed, from 1 January 2030 deferral by up to 5 years after reaching the statutory reference age will only be possible if gainful employment is continued and this is confirmed and proven in writing to the vested benefits foundation. For those born in 1965 or later, it is no longer possible to defer the withdrawal of vested benefits without proof of gainful employment. In order not to jeopardize planning security, the ordinance provides for a transitional arrangement for the period from 1 January 2024 to 31 December 2029 for all persons who wish to defer the withdrawal of vested benefits beyond the reference age. They can defer withdrawal during this period without proof of gainful employment.

Proof of gainful employment (from 1 January 2030)
To continue using your UBS Vested Benefits Account after reaching the reference age, you must submit a form confirming further gainful employment and proof of gainful employment to the UBS Vested Benefits Foundation. Further information will be provided at the appropriate time.

Early withdrawal of vested benefits
An early withdrawal can still be made at the earliest 5 years before reaching the reference age. In this case, you must fill out the form “ Payout UBS Vested Benefits Account ” and submit it to the UBS Vested Benefits Foundation.

General withdrawal options
General withdrawal options Regardless of the reason for the payout, please enclose the following documents: civil status certificate (issued no earlier than three months prior / marriage or civil partnership certificate) copy of the pension account holder's official form of ID with their signature copy of a spouse / registered partner's official form of ID with their signature Documents in a foreign language must be submitted with a certified translation in German, French, Italian or English. Send these and any other necessary documents to: UBS Vested Benefits Foundation AG Postfach CH-8098 Zurich You can request to withdraw your pension assets as early as five years before and as late as five years after you reach reference age . If you want to have your vested benefits paid out, send the completed and signed payout form to us at the above-mentioned address. If you plan to leave Switzerland permanently (you’ll neither be working nor living in Switzerland), you can request that your vested benefits be paid out. If you’re moving to an EU/EFTA country, generally only the supplementary portions of your pension assets can be withdrawn. If you are not subject to mandatory insurance in the country you are moving to, you can also withdraw the obligatory portion of your assets. A confirmation of this will be issued by the BVG Security Fund (available by going to www.verbindungsstelle.ch or by calling +41 31 380 79 71). If you’re moving to a country outside of the EU/EFTA (third country), you can withdraw all of your retirement assets. In addition to the payout form, one of the following certificates is also required to withdraw your pension assets upon leaving Switzerland: Deregistration notice from the Swiss resident’s registration office including the target country (deregistration date no earlier than one year prior) Residence certificate from abroad (date of issue no earlier than three months prior) Send all signed documents to the above-mentioned address. If you no longer work in Switzerland, making your cross-border commuter pass invalid, you can request that your pension assets be paid out. By doing so, you may no longer pursue employment in Switzerland nor have any place of residence in Switzerland. In addition to the payout form, the following document is also required to withdraw your pension assets when no longer working in Switzerland: confirmation of cross-border pass annulment Send all signed documents to the above-mentioned address.

General withdrawal options
In addition to the payout form, the following document is also required to withdraw your pension assets when no longer working in Switzerland: confirmation of cross-border pass annulment Send all signed documents to the above-mentioned address. If recipient of a full disability allowance from the Swiss Federal Invalidity Insurance, you can request the payout of pension assets. In addition to the payout form, the following document is also required to withdraw your pension assets following invalidity: a current Swiss Federal Invalidity Insurance confirmation (no older than one year) Send all signed documents to the above-mentioned address. If you become self-employed within a year and this is your main job, you can request that your pension assets be paid out. You must be self-employed in Switzerland and your business must either be a sole proprietorship or a partnership. In addition to the payout form, the following document is also required to withdraw your pension assets if you’re self-employed: AHV compensation office intake confirmation Send all signed documents to the above-mentioned address. If your assets with your most recent pension fund are lower than your personal pension contributions and you're not covered by any other pension fund, you can request that your pension assets be paid out. In addition to the payout form, the following document is also required to withdraw your pension assets in case of insufficiency: most recent pension fund statement Send all signed documents to the above-mentioned address. If a pension account holder dies, the pension assets will be given to the legal heirs. The assets will be paid out according to UBS Vested Benefits Foundation regulations. The assets will be paid out according to the order of beneficiaries if the pension account holder had drawn one up with the UBS Vested Benefits Foundation. In addition to the payout form, the following document is also required to withdraw pension assets in case of death: copy of the deceased pension account holder registered civil status document and/or a certificate of inheritance death certificate Send all signed documents to the above-mentioned address.

Withdrawing to buy real estate
If you’re buying a property, either in Switzerland or abroad, you can withdraw all or a part of your vested benefits for the scenarios highlighted below. You can withdraw money from each account(s) every five years until five years prior to you reaching reference age . You pay a fee of 300 Swiss francs per account. Financing a vacation home or a second home with your vested benefits is not permitted by law. The following documents are always required: civil status certificate (issued no earlier than three months prior / marriage or civil partnership certificate) copy of the pension account holder's official form of ID with their signature copy of a spouse / registered partner's official form of ID with their signature Documents in a foreign language must be submitted with a certified translation in German, French, Italian or English Send these and any other necessary signed documents to: Vested Benefits Foundation of UBS AG Postfach CH-8098 Zurich You can use your vested benefits to buy a home you plan to live in. In addition to the payout form, the following documents are required to withdraw your pension assets to buy your own home: officially notarized or a draft purchase agreement (no older than 3 months) use of funds confirmation from the mortgage creditor or notary (cf., payout form) consent to noting a selling restriction in the land register (cf., payout form) Send all signed documents to the above-mentioned address. If your desired home is under construction or still in the planning phase, you can use your vested benefits to finance it. In addition to the payout form, the following documents are also required to withdraw your pension assets when building your own home: extract from land registry (no older than 3 months) or an officially notarized purchase agreement for a piece of land (no older than 3 months) and a building loan or a draft of a purchase agreement for the piece of land and building services / architect contract use of funds confirmation from the mortgage creditor or notary (cf., payout form) consent to noting a selling restriction in the land register (cf., payout form) Send all signed documents to the above-mentioned address. You can use your vested benefits to repay your mortgage loan (amortization).

Withdrawing to buy real estate
You can use your vested benefits to repay your mortgage loan (amortization). In addition to the payout form, the following documents are also required to withdraw your pension assets to repay your mortgage loan: extract from land registry (no more than 3 months old) current residence certificate (no more than 3 months old) valid mortgage contract / confirmation from a mortgage creditor use of funds confirmation from the mortgage creditor or notary (cf., payout form) consent to noting a selling restriction in the land register (cf., payout form) Send all signed documents to the above-mentioned address. You can use your vested benefits to participate in financing a housing cooperative. In addition to the payout form, the following documents are also required to withdraw your pension assets to finance your participation in a housing cooperative / shares in a tenant public limited company: confirmation from the housing cooperative stating the number of shares (number and amount) rental contract QR-bill from the housing cooperative / tenant public limited company (payout to personal account not possible) Send all signed documents to the above-mentioned address. Renovations improve your home and increase its value, and you can use your vested benefits to finance them. You can find out more about the conditions of withdrawing your assets for renovation work in the fact sheet "Withdrawal for renovations". In addition to the payout form, the following documents are also required to withdraw your pension assets for home renovations: extract from land registry (no more than 3 months old) current residence certificate (no more than 3 months old) list of investments and detailed and signed order confirmations / statements (no more than 1 year old) consent to noting a selling restriction in the land register (cf., payout form) Send all signed documents to the above-mentioned address. A quick guide to ensure high security when 
using your card.
Whether you are traveling, in the shop around the corner or shopping online, you can play it safe by 
taking note of the following tips. When you get your card 
– Sign your UBS Credit / Prepaid Card and UBS Debit Card imme- diately on the reverse. – Learn your PIN by heart. – You can change your PIN at any ATM in Switzerland. Do not select easily identifiable combinations such as license plate num-
bers, dates of birth or telephone numbers, etc. For more safety from your card’s first use 
– Use a different PIN code for all cards 
– Conceal the keypad with your free hand or your wallet when typing in your PIN. – Keep your PIN secret and do not allow yourself to be watched while entering it. When you use your card at ATMs 
– Should your card be locked in a device, do not accept any help 
from unknown individuals. Inform the helpline immediately 
and have your card blocked. – Do not take any notice of any messages or notices that have been specifically attached to an ATM (for example, usage notices 
or faults). UBS does not attach notices to ATMs. – Before using an ATM, check to make sure no conspicuous or 
movable objects or covers are attached. If they are, do not 
withdraw any money, but report your observation to the affected 
bank or, if necessary, the police. – Wherever possible, use UBS ATMs for cash withdrawals, as they 
are subject to exemplary protection and monitoring from a tech-
nical perspective. When making purchases online 
– Check the terms and conditions before every purchase. – Never reveal your card number for information purposes only. – In principle, only make purchases online from companies that you trust. – Should your card be debited without delivery, let us know in writing within 30 days. – Check the billing amount and the retailer before sharing it using Access app or SMS code. Be suspicious of e-mail requests 
– Phishing is a sort of fraud involving the use of apparently repu- table e-mails, instant messages and Web sites. You will be asked 
for confidential and personal data. Never reveal any information! UBS will never ask you to reveal confidential personal data in this 
manner. – Give your mobile number to our Customer Services (by writing or 
via UBS Cards Online).

If you want to make a payment to another UBS Fisca 3a account, you can simply add it when selecting the beneficiary. From third-party providers Payment orders from third-party providers can be paid directly into the collective account of the Fisca Pension Fund Foundation: Credit account (IBAN): CH20 0023 0230 2480 3096 F Recipient: Fisca Vorsorgestiftung der UBS AG, 8098 Zurich Payment note: UBS Fisca 3a number / first name and last name of the UBS Fisca 3a account holder (e.g. F3xxxxxxxx / Max Muster) Attention: Please note the differing payment instructions for retroactive 3a payments . As long as you continue to earn an income subject to AHV contributions, you can still pay into pillar 3a after reaching normal AHV retirement age. Withdrawal of pillar 3a funds can also be deferred up to the age of 69 for women or 70 for men. Special case: deposits in the same year you retire If you continue to pay into the pension fund until you retire (e.g., until the end of April), you can pay the entire “small” amount into pillar 3a during this period. From May, you will still be employed but will no longer be paying pension fund contributions. From May to December, you may deposit an additional 20% of your net income into pillar 3a. However, you may not exceed the maximum amount that can be paid into pillar 3a. Can a part-time employee (e.g., 50%) who is obligated to make AHV contributions but is not a member of a pension fund still pay into pillar 3a? Yes, a part-time employee without BVG can also pay into pillar 3a up to a maximum of 20% of their (net) earned income, but no more than CHF 36,288 (from 2026). How much can part-time employees pay into the Fisca retirement savings account? If they are a member of a pension fund, employees can contribute up to the applicable statutory maximum amount for employed persons with BVG.

How much can part-time employees pay into the Fisca retirement savings account? If they are a member of a pension fund, employees can contribute up to the applicable statutory maximum amount for employed persons with BVG. If they are not a member of a pension fund, the relevant statutory amount is the same as that for self-employed persons, i.e., up to 20% of their (net) earned income, but no more than the statutory amount for persons without BVG. What is the maximum you can contribute when your BVG status changes? For self-employed workers, the amount may not exceed 20% of their annual salary from self-employment or the maximum amount allowed for persons without BVG. It does not matter whether the beneficiary takes up self-employment at the start of or during the course of the year. If the switch to becoming an employee, the maximum allowable for persons with BVG may not be exceeded. In total, your contribution may not exceed the maximum allowable for persons without BVG. Can beneficiaries pay contributions into pillar 3a if they are receiving unemployment benefits? Yes, because unemployment compensation counts as a substitute for earned income. The maximum amount may be deducted in the year that entitlement to unemployment benefit expires, even if this benefit has only been received for a few months (see Art. 7 para. 4 BVV 3). However, the annual unemployment benefit must be at least as much as the maximum amount for pillar 3a with BVG. You are not allowed to deduct contributions for amounts higher than the unemployment benefit itself. Furthermore, you must pay the maximum into your Fisca retirement savings account before your entitlement to unemployment benefit expires. As soon as your entitlement to unemployment benefit expires, your right to pay further contributions into pillar 3a does too, as you no longer have any income subject to AHV. Persons who are no longer entitled to receive benefits cannot make further contributions into pillar 3a unless they take up some form of employment (whether self-employment or employment). A person who is about to lose their entitlement to unemployment benefits, and who takes up self-employment in the same year, can deduct contributions to the Fisca retirement savings account in the amount of up to 20% of their self-employed income, or the maximum amount for beneficiaries without BVG if they are not affiliated to a pension fund.

Tax aspects An early withdrawal will result in the vested benefits being taxed in the year in which the withdrawal is made. If the pension account holder lives abroad or will leave Switzerland within a short time, a withholding taxes shall be levied. If the 
Foundation has no consistent information about the domicile (e.g. P.O. Box or c/o-address) a withholding tax will be levied as well. The Vested Benefits Foundation shall deduct these taxes directly from the UBS vested benefits account before paying out the pension 
benefits. The net amount paid out may therefore differ from the originally requested amount. In accordance with Art. 13 of the Ordinance on the Encouragement of the Use of Vested Pension Accruals for Home Ownership 
(hereinafter «WEFV»), the pension fund must report all early payouts of vested benefits and all repayments to the pension fund to the 
Swiss Federal Tax Administration using the relevant form within 30 days. The Swiss Federal Tax Administration keeps account of the reported early withdrawals and repayments of early withdrawals. Upon 
written request from the pension account holder, it shall confirm the amount of the outstanding early withdrawals and indicate which 
authorities are responsible for reimbursing the taxes paid. In the event of repayment of the advance withdrawal, the tax paid will be refunded excluding interest. In order for the taxes to be 
reimbursed, a written application must be sent to the authorities that levied the taxes. The pension account holder must submit a 
certificate authenticating the repayment of the pension capital invested in home ownership and of the taxes paid to the federal, 
cantonal and municipal authorities as a result of the early withdrawal (Art. 14 WEFV). Entitlement to reimbursement of the taxes paid 
shall expire three years after the early withdrawal has been repaid to the occupational pension plan (Art. 83a, para. 3 LPP). Ensuring proper use of the funds In accordance with the law, the Vested Benefits Foundation is obliged to submit a selling restriction to be annotated in the 
appropriate Land Register. It must do so when it pays out the early withdrawal. A property with a selling restriction cannot be sold 
without the consent of the Vested Benefit Foundation or the pension fund.

Beginning in 2021, it will no longer be possible to file requests for withholding tax adjustments on account of additional deductions (e.g. pillar 2 buy-ins, pillar 3a contributions or debt interest). 2020 is the last tax year for which a withholding tax adjustment can be requested. For this reason, you should check with your tax advisor whether it still makes financial sense to pay into a pillar 3a account starting in 2021. One change is that all withholding tax payers who live in Switzerland now have the option of a subsequent ordinary tax assessment. A request for withholding tax recalculation can only be made in isolated cases (e.g. if an incorrect rate was applied), but not to claim additional deductions. Additional deductions such as pillar 3a contributions can only be claimed under a subsequent ordinary tax assessment. If your gross annual earned income is at least CHF 120,000, you will continue to be subject to a subsequent ordinary tax assessment. Subsequent ordinary tax assessments will continue to be conducted until you are no longer liable for withholding tax. If your gross annual earned income is less than CHF 120,000, you can file a written request for subsequent ordinary tax assessment until 31 March of the year following the tax year. A request that has been submitted cannot be withdrawn and will apply until you are no longer liable for withholding tax. It is no longer possible to request a withholding tax adjustment. If you receive income that is not subject to withholding tax (e.g. returns from movable or immovable assets) in addition to your employment income, or if you have taxable assets (e.g. real estate), you were previously subject to a supplementary ordinary tax assessment. Beginning in 2021, a subsequent ordinary tax assessment will be mandatory in these cases for individuals who are liable for withholding tax. As a subsequent ordinary tax assessment may drive up or cut your tax bill, your tax advisor should check whether it makes sense in your case to request a subsequent ordinary tax assessment, especially depending on your place of residence. The short answer: to protect your accounts. For most payments, logging into the UBS TWINT App once with your password or biometric data will be enough. However, for security reasons additional authentication via the UBS Access App is required for certain payments. To confirm payments using the Access App, you must store your payment methods in UBS TWINT using your Digital Banking contract (Settings > Manage payment methods > Add/Update > with UBS Digital Banking contract) and activate the Access App. Without the Access App or a Digital Banking contract, you can only make payments within the defined limits. But with your Digital Banking contract and the Access App, you'll benefit from higher limits. Important: For security reasons, you only have 30 seconds to confirm UBS TWINT payments that require approval via the Access App.

Have you already installed the Access App?
Have you already installed the Access App? Please ensure that the Digital Banking contract from which the payment methods are taken is activated in the Access App. To do this, open the Access App and go to “Settings.” Add the relevant Digital Banking contract under “Manage access authorizations.”

Do you use a credit card that was not issued by UBS?
Do you use a credit card that was not issued by UBS? In this case, you cannot make payments of more than CHF 500. For security reasons, the transaction limit at some retailers is CHF 500. Would you like to increase your limit? Find all the information you need here .

You don't yet have the Access App?
You don't yet have the Access App? No problem. Download the Access App from the App Store or Google Play store here . Please note: If you have several UBS Digital Banking contracts, you need to set up the Access App for the contract whose payment methods you want to use in UBS TWINT. Only then can you use the Access App to confirm UBS TWINT payments.

On the weekend of 5 to 6 October 2024 , we have upgraded the IT infrastructure of the Fisca Pension Fund Foundation of UBS. We look forward to offering you an even better client experience in the future, starting with a new overview of your 3a retirement savings. The changeover has taken place automatically: you didn’t need to do anything.

General information on the Fisca changeover
Due to the change, your UBS Fisca accounts and associated UBS Fisca custody accounts have been assigned new combined Fisca 3a numbers. The new numbers replace your previous account and custody account numbers. They have been visible in your Digital Banking since 8 October 2024. Your 3a pension solutions are still listed in Digital Banking, at Multimats and on all Fisca documents. It is possible that a Fisca account or a Fisca custody account has been explicitly excluded from your Digital Banking contract. For legal reasons, the new combined retirement solution 3a (UBS Fisca 3a) cannot be displayed in Digital Banking. If you would like to see your UBS Fisca 3a account in Digital Banking, send your client advisor a message via the mailbox in E-Banking or call the hotline. Until the end of October 2024, you received an account statement from all Fisca accounts according to your delivery instructions, which includes the past transactions since the beginning of the year, as well as the balance. All balance views, as well as past transactions on former Fisca accounts, are not visible in Digital Banking. If you have any questions in this regard, you are welcome to contact your customer advisor or call customer service. Your 3a retirement savings accounts was debited and credited due to the changeover on the value date 4 October 2024 with the booking text “Transfer balance.” This ensured that the debit and the credit took place on the same date. Due to different “working hours” of the former and the new pension platform, the technical debit was completed on 7 October 2024 and the credit from 5 to 6 October 2024. Therefore, the booking date of the credit appeared as 5/6 October, and the debit on 7 October. The value date is relevant for the calculation of interest, so you were neither advantaged nor disadvantaged. You can download the amended regulations here at any time. Please note that the regulations have only been valid since 11 October 2024.

Administration
Due to the changeover, your Fisca accounts and associated Fisca custody accounts were assigned new, combined Fisca 3a numbers. The new numbers replaced your previous account and custody account numbers and have been visible in your Digital Banking since 8 October 2024. After the changeover, you also received a special statement with the new Fisca 3a numbers. Yes, the 3a retirement savings balance continues to be included in the total assets and is therefore relevant for the banking package price. No, we take care of the documentation and you don’t have to do anything. Existing general powers of attorney continue to apply to your 3a pension solutions at the Fisca Pension Fund Foundation. If you wish to revoke the power of attorney, please contact your client advisor. Yes, the existing beneficiary arrangement continues to apply after the changeover.

Opening and closing
You can continue to open a 3a pension solution yourself in Digital Banking. You can find out more at UBS key4 pension 3a . Newly opened UBS Fisca 3a will only be visible in Digital Banking the following day. However, payments in favor of newly opened UBS Fisca 3a can be recorded in Digital Banking immediately after the opening has been carried out. All forms and requests in connection with UBS Fisca 3a (disbursement requests, transfer forms, home ownership advances and more besides) can be found here .

Digital Banking
You will still find your 3a retirement savings in your Digital Banking under the home area on the “Accounts and cards” and the “Assets” tabs. Since the changeover in October 2024, no securities orders within pillar 3 are visible in the “Order overview” in Digital Banking. Pending securities orders already entered under pillar 3 have been displayed as “canceled” in the “Order overview” in Digital Banking. However, we have executed already registered securities orders according to your wishes. All Fisca documents can still be found in UBS Safe. Since the changeover, you will find the Fisca documents under the category “Important Information” and under the document type “Pension services.” Specific account names / abbreviations are assigned to Digital Banking contracts with up to 30 products. As soon as a Digital Banking contract contains more than 30 products, the additional account designations are assigned arbitrarily consisting of four digits. All account names / abbreviations can be changed independently in E-Banking under “Accounts & Cards” > “Account information.” All former Fisca accounts were netted between 8 October and 11 October 2024. As soon as a Fisca account, which has been set as a favorite on the home screen, has been balanced, the favorite will be displayed as “not available”. To change this view, the favorites can be updated or reset directly from the home screen.

Payments and standing orders
From UBS Nothing changes for you: You can still enter deposits in Digital Banking on the “Payments” tab. All available UBS Fisca 3a accounts already appear for selection within the same client relationship. Currency conversion
Currency conversion Every UBS card uses a certain currency – for example, most UBS cards issued in Switzerland use Swiss francs. When you use your card to make a payment in a different currency, for example when you are shopping in another country, you will be asked to choose between your card’s currency or the local currency. Then the payment will be converted at the exchange rate offered at the time of payment. This exchange rate will include a surcharge. Tip : Paying in local currency When you pay with a debit card in some hotels and stores abroad, you have the choice of paying the amount in Swiss francs or in the local currency. As a rule, it makes sense for you to opt for foreign currency. The conversion rates offered abroad are often based on a poor exchange rate. In some cases, exchange fees may also apply.

Information sheet
Reporting of a death Switzerland by the competent cantonal authorities. The death of a customer has to be reported to UBS Swit-
zerland AG (hereinafter “UBS”). A copy of the medical 
death certificate or an official death certificate is required 
for this purpose. Deaths can also be reported online:  
https://www.ubs.com/ch/en/help/account/case-of-
death.html. Rights of information Upon the death of a client, his heirs enter into the con-
tractual relationship with UBS as legal successors (excep-
tion see “Handling joint accounts”) In principle, each heir is entitled to information individu-
ally. In addition to the heirs, will executors and authorized 
representatives with an UBS “Power of attorney in inher-
itance cases” or an UBS “General power of attorney” 
also receive information, provided this has not been re-
voked. Rights to dispose In the event of death, the heirs form a community of 
heirs. Several heirs are only jointly entitled to dispose of 
the estate (overall relationship: exception see “Handling 
joint accounts”) Will executors have an exclusive right of disposal. Required identification documents for heirs 
and executors An original certificate of inheritance or a certified copy of 
the original is required. In Switzerland, the certificate of 
inheritance is issued by the competent cantonal author-
ities. All heirs must identify themselves with a certified copy of 
an official form of identification (passport or identity 
card). Certified copies of identity documents can be ob-
tained free of charge from all UBS offices in Switzerland. Will executors require an official executor’s certificate / 
official executor’s certificate, which is issued in The executor must identify himself with a certified copy 
of an official identity document. Power of attorney in inheritances cases If the community of heirs wishes to authorize one or 
more heirs of third parties to represent them vis-à-vis 
UBS, they must be issued with an UBS form “power of 
attorney in inheritance cases”. This power of attorney is 
issued by the client advisor. All heirs must be identified and sign the UBS form 
“power of attorney in inheritances cases”.

This power of attorney is 
issued by the client advisor. All heirs must be identified and sign the UBS form 
“power of attorney in inheritances cases”. Handling joint accounts («and-/or»- relation-
ships) According to the basic document for joint relationships 
(«and/or» relationship), the surviving contractual partner 
can continue to dispose of the assets of the joint busi-
ness relationship individually and without restriction. heirs who are not themselves contracting parties to the 
joint relationship do not enter into the contractual rela-
tionship with UBS and are not entitled to dispose of the 
assets. Legitimate heirs will, however, receive information 
about the assets up to the date of death. Handling collective accounts  
(«and»-relationships) According to the basic document for collective accounts 
(“and”-relationships), the heirs of a deceased contractual 
partner are subrogated to his rights. In this case, heirs and the surviving contractual partner 
can only dispose of the assets of the collective relation-
ship jointly. The singular form also includes the plural, and all masculine terms referring to persons refer to persons of both genders. Standing orders, LSV, cards Authorized representatives, heirs and executors can clar-
ify which orders or services exist in the deceased’s busi-
ness relationship and, if necessary, arrange for standing 
orders and LSV’s to be cancelled/adjusted or cards to be 
blocked. Heirs and executors are required to check exist-
ing powers of attorney and revoke them if necessary. Safe deposit box access Heirs are granted joint access to the safe deposit box. Ex-
ecutors and persons authorized with a “power of attor-
ney in in inheritance cases” are also granted access to 
the safe deposit box. Estate administrators, representatives of heirs, 
official liquidators If you have any questions about the identification docu-
ments and credentials of estate administrators, repre-
sentatives of heirs of official liquidators, please contact 
the client advisor. Ordering certificate of balance / asset state-
ment /tax statement as per date of death The certificates required in connection with the date of 
death can be obtained from the customer advisor or 
online at https://www.ubs.com/ch/en/help/account/case-
of-death.html. Certificates are generally sent the correspondence ad-
dress provided to UBS and usually take five bank working 
days.

You can manage signatories for a certain banking relationship yourself with just a few clicks in E-Banking, provided that you have signing authority for payment orders (individual or collective). Please note that the changes are only accepted and become visible after they have been processed. Log in to E-Banking. Go to “Settings > Signatories”. If there are multiple banking relationships, select the relevant banking relationship from the drop-down menu. Click “Add”. Enter the required data for the authorized signatory. Select the type of authorization (individual signatory authority / collective signatory authority). For collective signatory authority, check the grouping (if applicable). Confirm your entries. Click “Modify”. Modify the existing data of the authorized signatory. Confirm your entries. Click “Delete” for the person concerned. Confirm the withdrawal of signatory authority.
If you have authority to sign by joint signature , you can activate the confirmation of beneficiaries (payment recipients) yourself in E-Banking.

Activation
Activation Log in to E-Banking. Select "Settings > Are you already making full use of all the security options > Set up now/Security settings > Confirmation of beneficiaries". Activate the confirmation of beneficiaries for accounts with authority to sign by joint signature. The confirmation will be executed each time when entering the payment in E-Banking or in the Mobile Banking App.

Deactivation
The confirmation of beneficiaries can be deactivated at any time at the same place in the settings. You confirm the change with the Access Card and card reader or the Access Card Display, since you are dealing with an easing of the security settings.
